clue.text: Trump's nightly tweeting starts to get explosive

definitions.text: Trump's nightly tweeting starts to get explosive

parts.words: Trump's nightly tweeting starts to get explosive
parts.note: the starts of Trump's, nightly and tweeting are T, N, T, the familiar initials of the high explosive whose full chemical name is wanted

explanation.surface: A jibe that the US president's late-night social media posts are about to turn incendiary.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters spell the well-known abbreviation TNT; the grid wants the full chemical name it stands for, so the clue works as a cryptic definition rather than a letter-for-letter build.
explanation.definitionFit: TNT is the standard abbreviation of this yellow nitrated compound used in shells and demolition charges.

clue.text: Disturbance gent brought about in WC

definitions.note: W and C are the chemical symbols of the two elements in this hard compound

indicators.note: brought about suggests turning round and reshaping, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man causes a commotion in a public lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'WC' looks like a toilet, but it is the chemical formula: W (tungsten) and C (carbon).
explanation.definitionFit: The formula of this very hard compound of tungsten and carbon, used for cutting tools, is written with the symbols W and C.

clue.text: Isn't it possible a Python antihero's someone from Santander?

parts.note: isn't it possible is a roundabout way of saying it can't be, giving CANT
Brian is the reluctant hero of Monty Python's film Life of Brian

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a Monty Python character could hail from a Spanish port.
explanation.walkthrough: Life of Brian is a Monty Python comedy film whose title character is mistaken for the Messiah.
explanation.definitionFit: Santander is the capital of Cantabria, a region on Spain's north coast, so a native is a person of that region.

clue.text: Stepson embraces current love

indicators.note: embraces means the letters made from Stepson hold another piece inside them

parts.note: split as step plus son: a dance step is a PAS, then SON
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A man's stepson is hugging the person he currently loves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stepson' looks like one relative but is read as two words, step (PAS) and son.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong romantic or sexual desire for someone is a synonym for love.

clue.text: Novel Dune's not new? Indeed!

indicators.note: novel means fresh or new-made, so the letters of the title are recast
not tells us a letter is to be left out of the title's letters before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that their copy of Frank Herbert's novel Dune is second-hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a description of Dune but is the anagram signal; DUNES without N ('not new') gives DUES, rearranged. The whole clue then confirms the book is second-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-hand copy of a book is one that has been owned and read before, which the whole exclamation affirms.

clue.text: One might go off playing sex video with pelvic exercises at start

indicators.note: playing means the letters are set in motion and rearranged
at start means only the first letter of exercises is taken

explanation.surface: A racy-sounding fitness video mixing sex with pelvic floor workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two fodder words; E from 'exercises' is placed last.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb is designed to go off, so something that might go off describes it.

clue.text: As WC, perhaps, when in use periodically?

definitions.text: As WC, perhaps, when in use periodically?

parts.words: As WC, perhaps, when in use periodically?
parts.note: W and C are letters for tungsten and carbon in the periodic table of elements, so 'periodically' points to chemistry, not a toilet used now and then

explanation.surface: A question about how often a toilet gets used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' means 'on the periodic table', where W and C stand for elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Short letter codes such as W, C, Fe and Na stand for elements in the periodic table.

clue.text: Happy hour in pub right away leads to hugs and excitement

indicators.note: in places the rearranged hour within the shortened pub
away means the letter for right is taken out of the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: happy here is read as merry or tipsy, so the letters of hour are jumbled
leads means the opening letters of hugs and and are taken

explanation.surface: Happy hour at the local brings hugs and high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR loses its R ('right away') to give BA; 'Happy' turns HOUR into ROUH, which goes 'in' to make BROUHA; 'leads to' takes H and A from hugs and.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion or fuss is a burst of excitement.

clue.text: Intervals in boundary, closed with no U-turns

parts.note: in cricket a boundary hit over the rope without bouncing scores six

indicators.note: turns means the remaining letters are read backwards
with no tells us a letter is dropped from the word for closed

parts.note: shut means closed

explanation.surface: Sounds like a rule for a road or racetrack: no U-turns allowed within the closed boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: SHUT less U gives SHT, which 'turns' to THS. A cricket boundary is a hit worth four or six runs.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a sixth is the interval spanning six notes of the scale, such as C up to A.

clue.text: Sort of thinking lacking in man going overboard

indicators.note: sort of means a variety or rearrangement, so the letters of thinking are reordered
lacking tells us the letters of in are absent from the rearranged word

explanation.surface: A man going overboard is thinking in a muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: THINKING minus IN leaves THKNIG, rearranged. 'Man' is a chess piece; this one leaps over others on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess piece is called a man, and this one is the only piece that jumps over others as it moves across the board.

clue.text: Drying agent painter used in second East End abode

indicators.note: used in places the painter inside the Cockney home

parts.note: a Cockney from London's East End drops the H, so home becomes 'OME
Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A painter uses a desiccant in a second home in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional working-class district of London, whose Cockney accent drops the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: This mixture of caustic soda and quicklime absorbs moisture and carbon dioxide, so it is used as a desiccant.

clue.text: Small spud, but no King Edward in fact

indicators.note: but no means a piece is removed from the potato word

parts.note: tater is an informal word for a potato
ER, Edwardus Rex, is the royal cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: A small potato, but not in fact a King Edward variety.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, which makes it a neat decoy beside 'spud'.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistic, informally shortened, is a piece of factual data.

clue.text: Cissy with phobia, mostly about science

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and rearranged
mostly means the last letter of phobia is dropped

explanation.surface: A timid person with a phobia knows very little about science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims PHOBIA to PHOBI, which joins CISSY to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of living things using the methods of physics is a branch of science.

clue.text: Detective series given tip by Queen and Country

indicators.note: given by means the following pieces come after the tip
given by means the following pieces come after the tip

parts.note: a tip is a hint
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of a Queen
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A TV detective drama getting a pointer from the monarch and the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detective series' refers to the Welsh crime drama of this name, set around Aberystwyth.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a bilingual Welsh police drama broadcast on the BBC and S4C.

clue.text: Second cousin's mum's not a cop

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: not means the letter A is left out of the relative's name

parts.note: your cousin's mother is your aunt, or auntie

explanation.surface: Your second cousin's mother turns out not to be a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second cousin' looks like one relationship; Second is MO and cousin's mum is AUNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police is a police officer, informally a cop.

clue.text: Whines as Saint Bernard's sent back?

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: Bernard Levin was a British journalist and critic; his surname plus the possessive

explanation.surface: A dog's complaint about being returned, playing on the St Bernard breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint Bernard' looks like the dog breed but is S plus Bernard LEVIN's name, all reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To whimper or complain tearfully is to whine.

clue.text: Kill courier, showing mental problems …

parts.note: to hang someone is to kill them
UPS is a well-known parcel delivery company

explanation.surface: Wanting to murder the delivery driver reveals some psychological troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuroses or emotional inhibitions are informally called by this name.

clue.text: Moan made in wrong part of www.theguardian.com

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint has been posted on a faulty section of the Guardian's website.
explanation.definitionFit: The theguardian.com portion of a web address identifies the site on the internet.

clue.text: Times "Diary" is not even read here

indicators.note: not even means taking the odd letters, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A diary entry in the Times newspaper goes unread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the definition, as in periods.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods of the past, as in 'in olden days', are times.

clue.text: Like Inspector Clouseau's awful jewellery?

parts.note: bum is British slang for bad or worthless
bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A jab at the dreadful jewellery worn by the Pink Panther detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Clouseau is the clumsy French detective of the Pink Panther films.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouseau is famously clumsy and inept, which is exactly what the adjective describes.

clue.text: … 80% of that is due to 19 13 or 15

indicators.note: four fifths of the Latin phrase means only its first four of five letters are kept

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A fragment stating a percentage is owed to some numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with 19-across as 'days 13 or 15': in the Roman calendar the middle day of the month fell on the 13th or 15th.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar this was the 15th of March, May, July and October and the 13th of other months.

clue.text: Washbasin in toilet? A bowl wife left out

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a toilet

indicators.note: out means these letters are removed from bowl

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a washbasin belongs in the toilet, with a bowl the wife left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is an abbreviation here, not 'left behind': BOWL loses W and L to leave BO.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin for washing, originally the priest's handwashing basin in church, is a synonym.

clue.text: Highly-strung Edward, absorbed in self-reflection

indicators.note: absorbed in means the name sits inside the other piece
reflection means the word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: the ego is the self
Ned is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward is nervy and lost in introspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'self-reflection' reads as introspection, but splits into two jobs: 'reflection' turns the word for self round, and it 'absorbed' the short Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and nervous is a state of being highly strung.

clue.text: Disgraced ex-president loses temper at first, having lost in card game

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the shortened name
loses means a letter is taken away from the ex-president's name

parts.note: Augusto Pinochet was Chile's dictator-president, later disgraced over human rights abuses

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of temper

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A shamed former leader loses his temper after losing at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: PINOCHET 'loses' T ('temper at first') to give PINOCHE; L for lost goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: This trick-taking game for two to four players uses a 48-card pack.
